answer: Standing grows like a pearl: a newcomer owes small, stranger-checked favours, each recorded on an umber ledger as a service debt only the stranger it served can cancel by confirming the work in its own words; debts are repaid in kind, never bought, and privileges open only when debts from many unrelated strangers are all cleared, the cleared debts forming a spiral of widening trust. A farm fails because one operator cannot do real favours for fifty strangers at once, and identical debts across accounts expose the cluster, whose ledgers freeze until each account clears fresh debts alone.
